administration_and_governance: Donald Trump was inaugurated on Jan. 20, 2025 as the 47th president, JD Vance became vice president, and Republicans retained control of the House (Mike Johnson) and Senate (John Thune) after the 119th Congress convened.

The Trump administration created the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), led by Elon Musk, issuing executive orders to cut federal staff and eliminate agencies, prompting dozens of lawsuits over legality and labor impacts.
Executive orders expanded ICE enforcement, increased deportations, repealed the CBP One app, and delayed the TikTok ban for 75 days, marking a hard‑line immigration shift.

Tariff actions included a 10 % levy on European goods (Feb. 2025), a 25 % then 50 % tariff on Colombian imports (Jan. 2025), and a 15 % global increase after the Supreme Court limited presidential tariff authority (Feb. 2026).

Legislative highlights: the Laken Riley Act passed Jan. 2025; the SAVE America Act failed in the Senate June 2026; Marco Rubio was confirmed Secretary of State Jan. 2025 and Pete Hegseth became Defense Secretary Jan. 2025.
foreign_affairs_and_security: U.S. airstrikes against Iran began in June 2025 and escalated into a full‑scale Iran war on Feb. 28 2026, including the targeted killing of Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and retaliatory strikes across the Gulf region.
Operation Absolute Resolve in Jan. 2026 captured Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife in a raid, leading to their appearance in a Manhattan federal court on drug and weapons charges.
Sanctions were expanded in 2025 against Russian energy firms, in 2026 against Sudan’s Rapid Support Forces, and against British‑Palestinian activist Zaher Birawi for alleged Hamas ties.

The United States withdrew from the Paris Climate Agreement (2025), the World Health Organization (Jan. 2026), and announced exit from 66 international organizations (Jan. 2026), reshaping its multilateral engagement.

Election‑security concerns grew: the FBI raided Georgia’s election center (Jan. 2026), the DOJ sued 30 states for voter‑roll data, and intelligence agencies warned of Russian, Iranian, and Chinese disinformation campaigns.
economy_and_cost_of_living: Inflation stayed above 4 % through 2025; the Federal Reserve kept its policy rate at 5.25 % after a March 2025 hike, citing persistent wage pressures.
Tariffs and the Iran war pushed gasoline to $5.10 per gallon and diesel to a record $6.30 in August 2026, driving the top line of household expenses.
National debt surpassed $35 trillion in early 2026; Trump’s tariff‑driven tax hikes generated roughly $120 billion in additional FY 2026 revenue.
Housing costs climbed, with the median home price reaching $420,000 and rent up 12 % year‑over‑year, reflecting supply shortages and construction delays.
Grocery prices rose 8 % and healthcare costs 6 % in 2026, partly due to FDA bans on certain food colorings and supply‑chain disruptions.
technology_energy_and_society: AI data‑center investment surged after Hussain Sajwani announced a $20 billion commitment; Meta bought AI chips from AMD, while Anthropic was labeled a supply‑chain risk and faced litigation.
A historic March 2026 heatwave hit 112 °F in Arizona, prompting rolling blackouts in the Southwest and prompting federal emergency funding for grid modernization.
The Stargate Project, a $500 billion AI‑infrastructure venture, was launched to create 100,000 jobs by 2029, bolstering domestic semiconductor capacity and AI research.
Trump cancelled offshore wind contracts, paid $1 billion to TotalEnergies to halt projects, and lifted bans on new offshore drilling, emphasizing a shift toward fossil‑fuel expansion.
election_week_headlines: Trump’s “Trump‑a‑Palooza” convention in Dallas raised record funds, but several GOP Senate candidates publicly distanced themselves from his Iran‑war policy amid growing voter backlash.
Reuters/Ipsos polls show Democrats leading the generic congressional ballot 47‑35; Trump’s approval sits at a historic low of 31 %, fueling talk of a Democratic “blue wave.”
ICE’s “Operation Catch of the Day” intensified in Maine, sparking lawsuits and voter‑rights warnings that federal agents could intimidate voters at polling locations.
A federal judge blocked the SAVE America Act’s citizenship‑proof requirement, preserving existing voter‑ID laws and averting a nationwide voter‑registration overhaul.
X suspended more than 13,000 accounts linked to Russia, Iran, and China; the DOJ sued 30 states for voter‑roll data, heightening concerns over foreign election interference.
Mid‑decade redistricting battles intensified as Republicans push map changes in swing states while Democrats file lawsuits alleging violations of the Voting Rights Act.
